text.p: The following are the main stories from Monday morning's Austrian newspapers:

- Thaw in coalition relations ahead of a decision on the sale of Creditanstalt. The EA-Generali consortium is looking for another three billion schillings. The finance ministry will set a short deadline for changed bids.

- Austria's construction industry looks set to shrink again in 1997, the third successive year. A government attempt to kickstart the industry in the spring with new infrastructure projects has failed, according to research institute WIFO.
- The EA-Generali group bidding for the government's Creditanstalt stake is hoping Germany's Commerzbank and Italy's Banca Commerciale Italiana will put forward extra cash to raise the bid.
- Austrian lingerie firm Palmers plans to expand in the Middle East. In January Palmers will open a shop in Abu Dhabi and in March in Dubai.
- Steel firm VA Stahl is discussing a cooperation with Slovakia's VSZ, VA Stahl board director Wolfgang Eder said.

- Temporary truce in the coaltion war over Creditanstalt. The EA-Generali consortium wants to improve its bid. Finance Minister Viktor Klima is prepared to accept higher bids within a short period. Chancellor Franz Vraniztky says he does not expect a decision before early 1997.
- Pause for breath in Creditanstalt poker. In order to end a coalition crisis, the finance minister may be prepared to delay a sale decision beyond the new year.
- Austria Tabak expects a record two billion schillings cash flow this year and is looking for a wholesale partner. The state-owned firm is getting itself in shape for a stock exchange listing.
- Olympic 1,500 metre bronze medallist Theresia Kiesl and ski jumper Andi Goldberger were named sportsmen of the year
- Big stores have fared better than small shops in terms of Christmas trade.
- Creditanstalt sale decision unlikely before the middle of January.
